title: Multi-session longitudinal motor imagery EEG dataset (Kumar et al. 2024)
description: This dataset comprises multi-session longitudinal motor imagery EEG recordings from 18 BCI-naive subjects across six sessions (one offline, five online), designed to study transfer learning and BCI skill acquisition. It compares two domain adaptation frameworks—Generic Recentering and Personally Assisted Recentering—for calibration-free brain-computer interface training using left/right hand motor imagery with visual feedback. The dataset was converted to BIDS format via the MOABB pipeline and is hosted on NEMAR as part of a benchmark collection.
methods_description: EEG data were recorded from 18 healthy subjects using ANT Neuro eego mylab hardware with 22 EEG channels and 3 EOG channels at 512 Hz. Subjects performed cue-based left/right hand motor imagery tasks with continuous visual feedback across bar-feedback runs and car racing games. Session 1 consisted of 4 offline runs; sessions 2-6 included 3-4 online runs each. Signals were bandpass filtered (8-30 Hz) with second-order Butterworth filters, and covariance matrix features were classified using a Riemannian Minimum Distance to Mean decoder.
